_purpose: Frozen configuration of the bounded network-capacity comparison. Written and committed on 2026-10-04 BEFORE any of its models was trained or scored on the test or extrapolation sets. Do not change it after scoring; a change means a new, separately reported comparison.
question: Is the original 3 x 128 hidden-unit width a sensible capacity for the data-only network, compared with 3 x 64 and 3 x 192?
variant: data-only loss (physics = 0); the physics-loss comparison stays tied to the 3 x 128 network it was run on

training.checkpoint_rule: parameters at the epoch of lowest validation data MSE (as in the original runs)
training.data: data/flash_dataset.npz, the same grouped split by mixture, standardisation fitted on the training rows only

reused_runs.provenance_checked_by: python scripts/capacity.py provenance (epochs, batch, lr, hidden, physics, lambda, rows, dataset hash, torch version and threads must match this file)

selection_rule.statistic: for each width, the mean over seeds 0, 1, 2 of the best validation data MSE recorded during training (the checkpoint criterion)
selection_rule.rule: select the smallest width whose statistic is no more than 10 % above the lowest statistic among the three widths
selection_rule.why_10_percent: 10 % in MSE is about 5 % in RMSE. The seed-to-seed standard deviation of the best validation MSE of the original 3 x 128 runs is 0.15e-05 on a mean of 5.62e-05 (2.7 %, population std over seeds 0-2), so a 10 % difference is several times the training-run variability; a smaller difference is not treated as a benefit, and the smaller network is kept
selection_rule.test_data: not used: test and extrapolation results are reported for every width after selection and play no part in it

test_set_status: established benchmark: test-set results of the 3 x 128 models were already inspected and published (2026-09-21), so the test set is not a fresh holdout for this comparison; selection therefore uses validation data only
reported_for_every_width: training wall time of each run (machine and load recorded), and seconds per epoch measured for all widths on one machine in one session
inference time over the whole test set (median of 15 after 3 warm-ups, 2 threads)
training and validation MSE curves, best epoch, final training vs best validation MSE
test and extrapolation RMSE, MAE, R^2 and mean Rachford-Rice residual h^2
outputs: results/capacity/ (checkpoints, training records, capacity_results.json, capacity_table.csv, figure)
